newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government wins confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italian government wins confidence vote.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government won a confidence vote it called in the Senate (upper house) on Wednesday to sweep aside nearly 7,000 hostile amendments to a draft law on immigrants, parliamentary officials said.

The bill itself, which was approved by the Senate with the vote, must now move to the lower Chamber of Deputies, where the government may have to resort to another confidence call to overcome filibustering by hard right opponents.
The vote in favour of the motion in the Senate, where Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition enjoys a sizeable majority, was 163 to 106, parliamentary officials said.

The new law is designed to legalise the status of 250,000 foreigners who have applied for an amnesty since last November, when the then government issued a decree allowing illegal immigrants to stay as long as they registered with police.

The stop-gap measure, never converted into law, has been re-issued five times but cannot be rolled over again. The vacuum has raised doubts about whether foreigners who took advantage of the measures are now safe from possible expulsion.
The Constitutional Court last month banned the practice by which successive governments have re-issued decrees, which lapse after 60 days unless they are passed into law by parliament.
